claims.text: The targeted property for improvement in Fe-Co-Ni-based fcc high-entropy alloys is saturation magnetization (Ms).
The current scientific challenge is an inability to decouple orbital and spin magnetic moments in these alloys.
Strong crystal-field quenching suppresses the orbital magnetic moment in Fe-Co-Ni-based fcc alloys.
Complex multielement electronic hybridization prevents optimization of total magnetic moment through orbital engineering.
The total magnetic moment is represented as M = L + 2S.
The relevant Fe-Co-Ni-based high-entropy alloys have equimolar or near-equimolar compositions.
The initial alloys possess an fcc structure.
The initial alloys exhibit high ductility.
The initial alloys exhibit moderate saturation magnetization.
Adding small concentrations of Ru, Os, or Ta, or applying uniaxial strain, will break local cubic symmetry and enhance spin-orbit-coupling effects.
The proposed additions or strain can produce these effects without inducing phase separation.
Local symmetry breaking and d-band density-of-states changes near the Fermi level reduce crystal-field quenching.
Heavy-element addition or strain lifts d-orbital degeneracy.
Lifting d-orbital degeneracy permits partial recovery of the orbital moment.
The recovered orbital moment aligns with the spin moment.
Orbital-moment recovery can increase the total magnetic moment beyond the spin-only limit if hybridization does not cause antiferromagnetic coupling.
The intervention will increase both the orbital-to-spin moment ratio and saturation magnetization relative to an Fe-Co-Ni baseline.
The magnetic improvements will occur without a significant loss of ductility.
In the baseline Fe-Co-Ni fcc alloys, the orbital moment is approximately zero and saturation magnetization is determined almost exclusively by spin.

Composition, temperature, pressure, or alloy modification can destabilize a single-phase structure and promote competing fcc, hcp, BCC, or B2-containing states in transition-metal high-entropy alloys.
